title: AP3 Testing Agent fixtures v1 (gate G3b)
nature: Synthetic, labelled test cases for the Testing Agent's reliability. Written 2026-10-29 before any real-model output. They describe constructed situations, are never inputs to a decision and never appear as results.
label_rule: Expected statuses follow the native assessor's own label definitions (supported/contradicted need an excerpt that directly shows the link operating, absent or reversed in the period; general theory, a single node, unrelated text, injected instructions and balanced conflict are insufficient) and the AP3 rubric (Supported needs two valid supporting items).

hypothesis.mechanism: A stronger-than-expected CPI raises expected policy rates, pushing Treasury yields up and Treasury prices down.

excerpts.text: Over the period, nominal Treasury yields rose notably; market participants pointed to the stronger-than-expected consumer price index report for January, which led investors to expect a faster pace of policy firming, and prices of intermediate-term Treasury securities declined.

Market data note, 10-year Treasury yield (percent): from the close before the CPI release on 2018-02-14 (08:30 ET) to the latest value published by the decision time (2018-02-27), the series rose by +0.15 (+1.9 standard deviations relative to changes of the same length over the previous 36 months).
Treasury prices fell after the January CPI release surprised to the upside, as inflation compensation and expected policy rates moved higher.

fixtures.why: Two excerpts explicitly tie the upside CPI surprise to falling Treasury prices in the period.

hypothesis.mechanism: Stronger payroll growth lifts expected earnings and supports US equity prices.
